column2: Experienced hunters are often recruited into local formations of Caçadores due to their proficient at the use of the bow and arrow as well as superb quality as ambushers.

It is in those camps where the armies of northern Portugal train their 'Caretos', shock infantry formations who are often used to break the stalemate of battles and named after their use of the Caretos costume and their mask to strike fears into the hearts of their enemies.
It is in those camps where the armies of Iberia train their 'Rodeleros', shock infantry formations who are often used to break the stalemate of battles and named after their use of the Rodela shield.

Andalusian horses are renowed all over the world as some of the best cavalry in the world, a fact which doesn't go unnoticed by Andalusians nobles, who take their sons young age to the equestrian schools where they learn from a young age the art of riding those formidable horses.
Similar to their Andalusian neighbors, the Alentejanos have adapted to fighting on horsebacks by harassing and flanking the enemies and then feigning retreats.

Heavily armed with battle axes and armoured with plumed helmets, the Sapeurs de la Garde specialize in military engineering and underground combat, though they can also serve as an elite corps of provisional infantry.

Skilled sailors and consummate ambushers, the mariners of Brittany's coasts are as fearless on land as on sea. Whether it is a quick strike on an undefended target or a more protacted battle, they shall respond to the call. Kentoc'h mervel!

These isolated camps, usually in the forest, provide the perfect locale for the lifeblood of Welsh and Cornish sovereignty, where they could train, produce weaponry for their militia and learn to live off the land, away from the prying eyes of lords and kings, be they foreign or domestic.

Albeit Leagues were once spoken of a sport that caused peasants to go mad and cause immense damage, these Leaguers are war camps established by British lords to hone and prepare men who would use the halberd-like weaponry to wild success against both raiders from the rest of the Isles and foreign conquerors who dared to enter a struggle against Queen and Country.

The schiltron is a compact body of Scottish pikemen. If threatened by cavalry, they present row upon row of spears firmly braced in the earth. Only a fool or a madman would willingly charge into such a dense wall of killing instruments.

Civilian housing repurposed for the residence of these plaid-laden, barefooted warriors, primarily with the peasantry in them still. They are primarily displeased at them, but aren't to complain due to their extreme resilience even in the coldest weather and the fact that they are armed troops.

The Gewalthaufen is a shambling mass of pikes and halberds, the men usually protected by a ridged helmet and a cuirass. Flags, drums and horns coordinate the formation so that the officers with with decorated helmets can move hundreds of men with one word. This of course needs a rather high amount of training and equipment which is why the local authorities like to keep a training ground and a stockpile of equipment around.

The German low-lands are a place where cavalry is king. These men and their steeds are equipped with the best arms and armour they can afford. Of course the ones that serve a rich lord are usually better armed but all of them usually have a common area where they can make sure that their horses are being taken good care of.

Serving both in peace as well during war, the Carabinieri keep order in the countryside, the army camp and the battlefield. But to to think of them as bailiffs with plumed helmets is a mistake an enemy makes only once.

The Bersaglieri are lightly armed but not to be taken lightly. These men easily flank any footmen and fall in their backs with devastating results. Not many are taken into their ranks as their speed on foot is something that needs a lot of training, which may be another reason why the merchant class is rather absent from their ranks.

The sipahi are professional light cavalry, holding fiefs in the name of the local lord. Armed with round shield, lance, javelin and light armour, they excel at lightning-fast strikes and harrassing enemy troops.

Masters of Kurdistan's rugged and inhospitable terrain, Peshmerga fighters have stood watch over the mountains for centuries. Their name translates to "those who stand in front of death", and indeed, any enemy crossing into their territory shall sure find out why.

The Caucasus' mountains are a harsh place, but it is the one those hardy mountaineers call home. Clad in cherkesskas, heavy fur hats and equipped with long blades, they are astute defenders of the land.

This fortified monastery is defended by regiment of sturdy Romanian falx-wielders. Their long two-handed blades, with the inner edge sharpened, have been known to take off limbs and even heads in one blow!
Known for their distinctive dress and especially the fustanella, a sort of long skirt, these soldiers have guarded the lords and ladies of Hellas for centuries and shall do so forevermore.
The hussars make excellent light cavalry, and are trained to hit the enemy relentlessly from different directions before regrouping and doing it again.

The Carpathians' lofty peaks are home to rough warriors and soldiers. Though their equipment is of varying quality and the protection they can afford has its up and downs, nobody can doubt these hardy highlanders' courage.
These urban militias are named after the Flemish goedendag mace they favor in battle. They have proven themselves more than once against armored cavalry.
